title: Right-heart signs in a young adult / Confirm the haemodynamics and assess risk

blocks.text: Right-heart signs in a young adult / Confirm the haemodynamics and assess risk

AMaC MRCP PACES · R5-114 · Physical examination · PACES Station 3, cardiovascular · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 minutes (up to 6 examination, at least 4 questions) · Guideline dates and links in section 15 · Related AMaC: condition may appear elsewhere in a different context.
A young adult woman has progressive exertional breathlessness. Examine the cardiovascular system to establish the cause and outline the next steps.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text:
HOOK — Loud P2 and an RV heave indicate pulmonary hypertension; idiopathic PAH is a diagnosis after haemodynamic confirmation and exclusion of other causes.
EXAMINER TRAP — Do not pronounce idiopathic PAH from auscultation or echocardiography alone, or disregard pregnancy risks.

blocks.text: Not applicable — physical examination encounter. Patient is cooperative, answers simple comfort or symptom questions; no communication surrogate.

RELEASED FINDINGS — on inspection, pulse, precordial palpation and auscultation as appropriate: Prominent right ventricular heave, loud P2, raised JVP with mild oedema, no left-sided murmur, no crackles; stable at rest.
Question 1 [R4] — Can examination prove idiopathic PAH? | No; catheterisation and exclusion of secondary PH required.
Question 2 [R5] — Next investigations? | Echo, V/Q, lung tests, serology and right-heart catheterisation at PH centre.
Question 3 [R6] — Red flags? | Syncope, RV failure or rapid decline.
Question 4 [R7] — Pregnancy? | High risk; specialist shared counselling and contraception advice.
Curveball — If a candidate asks for definitive proof from examination alone: “Explain what examination suggests and which confirmatory tests you need.”

Loud P2 and an RV heave indicate pulmonary hypertension; idiopathic PAH is a diagnosis after haemodynamic confirmation and exclusion of other causes. Do not pronounce idiopathic PAH from auscultation or echocardiography alone, or disregard pregnancy risks. No; catheterisation and exclusion of secondary PH required. Echo, V/Q, lung tests, serology and right-heart catheterisation at PH centre. Syncope, RV failure or rapid decline.

THINK: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension.
SAY: Loud P2 and an RV heave indicate pulmonary hypertension; idiopathic PAH is a diagnosis after haemodynamic confirmation and exclusion of other causes.
DO: Consent, focused cardiovascular examination, present findings and next tests.
NUMBERS: 10-minute examination encounter (PACES23).
TRAP: Do not pronounce idiopathic PAH from auscultation or echocardiography alone, or disregard pregnancy risks.
FINISH: Explain definitive investigations and appropriate specialist follow-up.
